title: Password reset validation leaks registered email addresses
reasoning: PasswordResetSerializer returns a distinct validation error when no User exists for the submitted email. On a public password-reset endpoint this allows account enumeration by comparing API responses for registered and unregistered addresses. The included email-template tests cover rendering the reset email, but they do not establish that the reset request endpoint should reveal existence.
recommendation: Make password-reset request validation response generic regardless of whether a matching user exists, and only send email when a user is found. Keep detailed logging server-side if needed.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included password-reset tests only render templates and check content. They do not assert API behavior for unknown emails or response indistinguishability.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add serializer or endpoint tests asserting the same success response/status for existing and non-existing email addresses while verifying mail is sent only for existing users.
minimumFixScope: hub/serializers.py PasswordResetSerializer.validate_email and the caller’s handling of the no-user case.
